name: Ceara
summary_text: Ceará is the most consistent lethal hotspot for trans and travesti people in the Northeast: 11 killings in 2024 (3rd nationally, 1st in the region) and 8 in 2025 (tied for the highest state total in the country). Against a population of ~9 million this yields roughly 0.9 killings per million per year—more than double the national rate of ~0.38/million (80 / 213 M). The 2025 dossier further notes a concentration of Black victims in Ceará. This places Ceará about 0.10 below the national 0.71. The deviation is driven by sustained, patterned lethal exposure rather than any legal distinction (the federal constitution and penal code apply uniformly). Compared with Minas Gerais (0.64), which matched Ceará's absolute 2025 count of 8, Minas Gerais' much larger population (~21 M) gives a per-capita rate at the national average, making Ceará the higher-risk state on a rate basis. For a visibly trans visitor, the pattern matters: the killings are concentrated on young Black trans women in public space—precisely the exposure profile of a conspicuous traveller—and the consistency across two years signals an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip.

sources.title: Ceará lidera assassinatos de pessoas trans em 2025; no Brasil, maioria das vítimas são negras – Igbá Agência
sources.claim_summary: Igbá Agência report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th ANTRA dossier: Ceará recorded 8 killings of trans people in 2025, tied with Minas Gerais at the top of the state ranking; Brazil total 80 — 18th consecutive year as the country killing the most trans people; of the 57 cases with race recorded, 40 (70%) were Black; the Northeast took 38 of 80; killings fell ~34% from 122 in 2024, which the dossier attributes to violence migrating into attempted homicides rather than to improvement.

sources.title: Brasil lidera ranking mundial de assassinatos de pessoas trans | SBT News
sources.claim_summary: SBT News dossier report: ANTRA recorded 80 killings in 2025 (down 34% on 2024, no improvement per ANTRA's president given rising attempted homicides); 97% of victims were travestis and trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% Black; 67.5% of killings happened outside state capitals; cumulative 2017-2025 shows 1,261 killings (~140/year) with Ceará in the top tier of states; Brazil has led the global tally since 2008 per the TvT Trans Murder Monitoring observatory.
